preview: Madhura Sawant's interview and internship experience at Citi, detailing the online test, technical interview, HR round, and the 8-week internship leading to a PPO.
content: Interview and Internship Experience Madhura Sawant Information Technology(2024) CGPA: 6+ STIPEND: 75k LOCATION: PUNE PPT The PPT was conducted on 6th September 2022. Make sure you are attending the ppt as it might help you answer questions about the company. In my situation, during the technical interview's conclusion, the interviewer inquired if I had attended the PPT, as I had asked a question about Citi's work culture :) Online Test (11th September) The online test was conducted on the AMCAT platform. The test had 5 sections (You cannot navigate back to previous questions and also are unable to switch between sections): 1. CS-based MCQs (25 Questions in 35 minutes) 2. Aptitude(16 Questions in 16 minutes) 3. Logical Reasoning (14 Questions in 14 minutes) 4. Verbal Reasoning (22 Questions in 18 minutes) 5. Coding Section (2 questions in 1 hour) Coding Section: There were different sets of questions for everyone 1 easy and 1 medium type. The first question for me was to find the GCD of the array elements. I was able to pass all the test cases for this question. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/gcd-two-array-numbers/ I don’t exactly remember the second question, but the situation was given like this: You are given a pipeline network through which oil flows from a source node to a sink node. The pipeline network consists of nodes and directed edges connecting these nodes, representing the pipes through which oil can flow. Each pipe has a certain capacity that defines the maximum amount of oil it can transport per unit of time. Your task is to determine the maximum amount of oil that can be transported from the source node to the sink node per unit of time, considering the capacities of the pipes and the flow constraints. The goal is to optimize the flow such that the maximum amount of oil is transported from the source to the sink. So this question was based on graphs and I only passed 9/15 test cases. From the online tests, 76 students were shortlisted for the interviews. Technical Interview (14th September) My interview was scheduled for 10 am and was being conducted online through Zoom. It was a 30 mins interview as expected and the interviewer was very nice and friendly. He started with the typical ‘tell me about yourself’ question. In my introduction, he asked me about the college clubs that I was a part of at that time. After that, he asked 2 puzzles one of which I was able to answer correctly. Then he asked me a question based on probability. I was nervous about my response since I wasn't sure of the answer. But he calmly guided me, and I managed to answer it afterwards. Then he asked me what is recursion and state some problems that can be solved using recursion except for finding the power of a number. So I stated that we can solve factorial and fibonacci series using recursion. He was not satisfied with the answer and asked me to tell him some other problem. At that moment, nothing came to my mind except dynamic programming, so I answered that we can solve the subset sum problem using recursion and dynamic programming. He asked me what is dynamic programming and the approach and psuedocode to solve the subset sum problem. Further, he asked me some questions in DBMS and a few SQL queries. He asked me which social media I used the most, so I replied Instagram. On this, he asked me what kind of database Instagram used and its advantages and if I was about to create a social media app how would I design the schema for its database. He asked me to describe a schema for both structured and graph databases and which one was better for the app. I answered for both and he seemed quite satisfied with it. Then I was asked to explain the difference between paging and segmentation. Lastly, he asked me to tell him about a software that I use and what can be improved in that. Again, I was blank and only thought of Instagram :P So I told him about a feature which I thought can be improved but he questioned me on its feasibility and what will be my approach to improving that for which I had a very vague answer and didn’t seem to satisfy him. Finally, he asked me if I had any questions and the interview was concluded (Make sure you have something to ask that makes sense). I did not expect that I’ll be selected for the next round but fortunately, I was called for the next round within a few minutes. HR Interview (14th September) My HR interview was scheduled at 11.30 am and it lasted about 30 mins. This round also began with an introduction, first HR then me. He asked me about all my projects. For explaining the project I used the STAR approach. Later, he requested a detailed explanation of my most recent project, and this discussion continued for a considerable amount of time. Because this was a group project he asked me about my contribution, what tech stack did we use and why. He asked me to explain the complete workflow of the project: How did we plan the workflow? How was the work divided and on what basis? Were we able to execute everything and what was left for future scope? I explained that the project's dataset wasn't readily available and that we had to create one. Consequently, I found myself facing a barrage of questions related to DBMS once again. I mentioned that we were using both MongoDB and Firebase in the project and that I had worked on Firebase so he asked me to compare Firebase and MongoDB and which one I found better. Later on, he asked me a few questions on the front end. I thought the HR seemed content with my answers, which helped me feel more at ease for the rest of the interview. After this he asked me about my hobbies, what I liked about the college and what are my future plans after I complete the degree. In the end, he inquired if I had any questions, and I took the opportunity to ask about the requirements for the projects interns receive and the technologies available for interns to explore. As we were finishing the conversation, he shared that he works in the Pune office and hinted at the possibility of us meeting if I get selected, this really made me hopeful about my chances of being chosen. Around 10 pm that day, the results were announced, and I felt fortunate to be among the 15 students who were selected :) Internship Experience (29th May’23 - 21st July’23) So this was an 8-week long internship in Kharadi, Pune. I was placed in a team of 16 interns under the same manager in the Equities department. We were assigned two projects, and each of them had to be completed. As a result, we were divided into two teams, each consisting of 8 members. The projects were completely different one was a Realtime System performance tracker and the other was Log analysis, spam detection and standardization. The first project required Java as the backend while the second project required Python due to its focus on machine learning. I opted for the second project for two main reasons: firstly, my proficiency in Java was at a beginner's level, and secondly, I had recently studied machine learning in the previous semester. The project we worked on had many features to add, so once again, we split into groups based on these features. I along with another teammate worked on the error and exception-handling part of logs where we created and trained a model that will classify logs into different error categories. The most challenging part here was generating a dataset for model training, selecting the suitable model (which consumed a significant portion of our time as we switched between two models), and then testing this model on files containing around 3 million logs :) I partnered with another teammate to work on developing the frontend of our project. Along with this I also volunteered for documenting our project on Confluence. Apart from the technical knowledge, my internship at Citi provided valuable insights into teamwork and communication. Being active in scrum meetings allowed me to closely engage with my team members, plan the workflow, discuss challenges and upcoming tasks, and efficiently track our project's progress. The work environment at Citi is remarkably friendly, and everyone is enthusiastic about assisting - you just need to reach out and ask. Talking about our project in meetings with senior team members made me feel more confident. And in the end, this is what truly matters! Finally, at the end of the week after the internship concluded, we received the pre-placement offers (PPOs), and I was among the ones who secured a PPO. To sum it up, this journey has been truly amazing and I would like to thank VJTI TPO and CITI for providing this wonderful opportunity. Resources 1. For DSA I initially followed 450 DSA Cracker and then Striver’s SDE sheet. Youtube channels which I followed: Take U Forward, Abdul Bari (for algorithms), Aditya Verma (for DP). 2. For OS and DBMS, I mostly followed my notes made during the sems and last-minute notes on GFG. 3. For OOPs I followed Interviewbit. 4. For HR questions also I followed the Interviewbit website ALL THE BEST !!!
